top_news.title: Automating coherent long-form video generation
top_news.dek: Google Research addresses semantic drift and cascading failures in long-form video generation pipelines.
top_news.brief: Current video diffusion models struggle to maintain consistency across long-form content. Google is investigating how to mitigate semantic drift and cascading failures that occur when chaining independent modules, aiming to improve the reliability of automated storytelling engines.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing video diffusion pipeline modules

top_news.title: Framing by Wording, Framing by Selection: A Large-Scale Two-Dimensional Audit of French News Headlines, 2022-2025
top_news.dek: Researchers propose a two-dimensional framework to decouple salience framing from selection framing in news headlines.
top_news.brief: Current computational methods often conflate how news is worded with what is selected for coverage. This new framework separates salience (measured via loaded vocabulary, blame, and rhetorical devices) from selection (measured via outlet-level story distributions). The study utilizes a 10,000-headline French dataset annotated by LLMs to provide a more granular audit of media bias.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing the two-dimensional axis of news framing: salience versus selection.

top_news.title: White House tells OpenAI and Anthropic to let U.S. review new models before sharing them with British testers
top_news.dek: The White House has requested that OpenAI and Anthropic prioritize U.S. government reviews of new AI models over sharing them with U.K. testers.
top_news.brief: The Office of the National Cyber Director is pressuring leading AI labs to withhold new models from the U.K.'s AI Safety Institute until U.S. agencies have completed their own evaluations. This directive forces companies to navigate conflicting international regulatory expectations, with Anthropic reportedly complying by delaying model access for British partners.
top_news.image_alt: Conceptual graphic representing U.S. and U.K. regulatory oversight of AI development.

top_news.title: Fastino Releases GLiNER2.5-Decide: A 340M Open-Weight Decision Model That Runs on CPU
top_news.dek: Fastino Labs released GLiNER2.5-Decide, a 340M-parameter model optimized for agentic decision-making tasks.
top_news.brief: Designed for routing, triage, and tool selection, this open-weight model outputs structured answers with probability distributions and confidence scores. It is Apache 2.0 licensed, runs on standard CPUs, and is intended for integration into agent pipelines requiring low-latency, reliable judgment calls.
top_news.image_alt: Technical architecture diagram of the GLiNER2.5-Decide decision pipeline.

top_news.title: Runway’s WorldPrompt and the Engineering of Real-Time Worlds
top_news.dek: Runway's GWM Worlds 2 introduces WorldPrompt, a format for controlling real-time interactive simulations.
top_news.brief: Runway's latest research preview uses an autoregressive diffusion approach to enable real-time video and audio generation. The WorldPrompt feature allows developers to anchor specific environment states and inject timestamped events, effectively turning high-fidelity generative models into interactive, steerable simulations.
top_news.image_alt: Visualization of a real-time generated simulation environment controlled by WorldPrompt.

primary.title: AI performance costs are falling faster than those of any previous technology
primary.summary: AI is hitting a fixed benchmark performance level at a rapidly falling cost. Epoch AI measures a price decline of about 13x per year. After stripping out hardware gains and competition, MIT puts annual algorithmic progress at about 3x. That doesn't mean today's best models are cheaper, though. Reasoning models, for example, can cost more because they use far more compute per task. When picking a model for real-world use, quality, speed, and error rate matter just as much as price. primary.title: Contrastive-LM Releases CLM-8B: An Open System One Model That Scores Agent Actions Up to 9× Faster Than Jev
primary.summary: Contrastive-LM has released CLM-8B, an open System One model that scores candidate actions against a state instead of generating text. It adds 2 small projection heads to a frozen Qwen3-8B encoder and trains them with a contrastive InfoNCE objective. In zero-shot tests it runs up to 9× faster than TypeSafe's Jev. With fine-tuned heads as a verifier, it reaches 81.6% on held-out DeepSWE tasks and 87.6% on held-out Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks. The post Contrastive-LM Releases CLM-8B: An Open System One Model That Scores Agent Actions Up to 9× Faster Than Jev appeared first on MarkTechPost.
